title: Half-Open Ranges
hints: There is no `n` and no index here. Walk a pointer: `for (const int* p = first; p != last; ++p)`. The loop never runs when `first == last`, which is exactly what an empty range needs.
In `find_in_range`, return `p` the moment `*p == target`. If the loop finishes, return `last`, not `nullptr`. Never read `*last`: it is one past the end.
